page: Amazon Web Services r8a.12xlarge is an eighth-generation memory-optimized instance powered by the AWS Nitro System and dedicated AMD EPYC 9R45 processors. Operating on the x86_64 architecture at clock speeds reaching 4.5 GHz, this configuration provides 48 physical cores mapped to 48 vCPUs with a single thread per core execution model. It includes 384 GB of DDR5 system memory clocked at 6 GHz, establishing an 8:1 RAM-to-vCPU ratio. Network connectivity is supported by a 22 Gbps baseline interface. The instance does not include bundled local storage or dedicated hardware GPU accelerators, necessitating remote block storage solutions for persistent data workloads.

Benchmark results demonstrate top-tier execution across compute and memory subsystems. In computational throughput, the instance achieved a multi-core score of 29928 on Geekbench and 102262.64 on PassMark CPU, supported by an extended instruction set featuring AVX-512 vector extensions. Memory throughput reached 10047.06 GB/sec in small block cached reads and 176.08 GB/sec in large block uncached writes. Database handling capabilities registered 41572.76 on the PassMark database operations test, alongside 154.63 million operations per second during Redis SET testing. CPU-based machine learning inference recorded 338.54 tokens per second on small models and 55.03 tokens per second for medium model text generation.

From a cost-efficiency and system architectural perspective, the 1:1 physical core allocation eliminates hyper-threading contention, maximizing predictable per-core execution. The DDR5 memory bandwidth and large L3 cache structure support high-density in-memory processing. However, the lack of integrated local NVMe storage introduces latency and bandwidth dependencies on external storage attachments for high-throughput persistent I/O. The r8a.12xlarge is suited for in-memory databases, large-scale Redis caching tiers, distributed real-time data analytics, and enterprise memory-intensive applications requiring substantial RAM allocation.
description: Amazon Web Services r8a.12xlarge is a memory-optimized Nitro hypervisor instance powered by dedicated AMD EPYC 9R45 processors running at 4.5 GHz. Featuring 48 physical cores and 48 vCPUs on the x86_64 architecture, it delivers 384 GB of high-speed 6 GHz DDR5 memory, yielding an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio. The server features a 22 Gbps baseline network capacity but contains no local storage or GPU accelerators. In benchmarks, it shows exceptional multi-core computational performance and high memory bandwidth, scoring 102262.64 on PassMark CPU and processing over 154 million Redis SET operations per second. The elimination of simultaneous multithreading provides consistent compute predictability across all cores. The r8a.12xlarge is suited for memory-intensive workloads, including large-scale in-memory databases, memory caching tiers, data analytics engines, and high-concurrency enterprise applications.
